title: USS Cod (SS-224)
description: Gato-class fleet submarine, seven war patrols, a memorial on the Cleveland waterfront since 1976.
content:
Cod is a Gato-class fleet submarine, built at Electric Boat in Groton, Connecticut, and commissioned in June 1943. She made seven war patrols in the Pacific, sank more than a dozen ships including the destroyer Karukaya, and in July 1945 rescued the entire crew of the Dutch submarine O-19 from Ladd Reef, the only submarine-to-submarine rescue in history.

She came to Cleveland in 1959 as a Naval Reserve training ship and has been a memorial on the Lake Erie waterfront since 1976. She is the only WWII submarine open to the public that has never had stairways or doors cut into her hull. You board her the way her crew did.

The USS Cod Submarine Memorial keeps her afloat and open, daily from May through September. For hours, tickets, and events, see usscod.org.

title: About these answers
description: Where the answers come from, and who wrote them.
content:
The questions and answers on this page were written by submarinedocent.org from published sources: the Dictionary of American Naval Fighting Ships, the Memorial's own history at usscod.org, and Paul Farace's account of the O-19 rescue. Each answer cites its source. If you find an error, the “Share your feedback” link on any answer reaches us directly, and corrections from the Memorial are welcome.
